steps.body: One amount wears three costumes: the numeral 4, the word “four”, and a picture of four things. All name the same count.
steps.narration: One amount wears three costumes: the numeral 4, the word “four”, and a picture of four things. All name the same count.

widget.prompt: The word says “four”. Build the amount all three costumes share.

commonCounts.feedback: Three misses the shared amount; every costume of four names one more.
Five overshoots; the word four, the mark 4, and the picture all stop together.

widget.missFeedback: Whatever the costume, build the one amount it names.
widget.successFeedback: Four — word, mark, and picture agree, because underneath they are one count.

predict.prompt: Numeral 4, word “four”, picture of 4 dots — how many amounts?
predict.reveal: The costumes differ; the count underneath is the same single four.

cml.actionGoal: Link the written numeral to the exact amount it names for kcw three forms.
invariants: A numeral is a written promise about an amount: it records the last word of a careful count, position gives each digit its job, and the promise survives any change of objects or arrangement — the anchor for kcw three forms.
misconceptions: Treating numerals as decorations, reading digit pairs without position, or matching a numeral to roughly rather than exactly its amount.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If one more thing joined the group, which single mark of the numeral would have to change?

widget.prompt: Numeral 4, the word “four”, and a picture of 4 dots — how are they related?

options.label: Three different numbers
options.feedback: They differ in costume only; underneath, each says exactly four.

options.label: Three ways of writing one same amount
options.feedback: Correct — mark, word, and picture all name the identical count of four.

options.label: The picture is the biggest
options.feedback: Pictures take more space, but space is not amount — all three say four.

options.label: Only the numeral is real
options.feedback: All three are real names; the numeral is just the fastest to write.

hints: Last number said, first mark written.

widget.prompt: A group shows 6 dots. Which numeral names that amount?

options.feedback: 7 promises more dots than the group holds; the count stops at 6.
5 promises fewer dots than the group holds; the count reaches 6.
Correct — the numeral 6 is the written name for a group of exactly 6.
8 promises more dots than the group holds; the count stops at 6.

widget.prompt: What number comes right after 6? Hop one and tap where you land.

commonLandings.feedback: 6 stops one complete hop too soon. Continue the final 1-unit hop to reach 7.
8 goes one complete hop too far. One hop from 6 lands on 7.

widget.missFeedback: Count 1 on from 6: you land on 7.
widget.successFeedback: 7 — the next numeral in the writing order is the next number in the song.
widget.lowFeedback: Short of the landing — a single hop forward reaches 7.
widget.highFeedback: Past the landing — right after 6 means one hop, stopping on 7.
